To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the formalization and integration of documents and collections from Software Engineering projects can be supported with the use of RDFa, (ii) this formalization can be used for enabling multi-dimensional document browsing, (iii) it can be used for exporting the formalized knowledge to the Semantic Web.

(a) RDFa-based extensions to MKM formats are well-suited for encoding the multi-dimensional classification of documents and collections; (b) these extensions can be used for interactive document browsing, metadata query over documents and collections and for exporting Linked Open Data to the Semantic-Web.
RDFa-based metadata extensions of MKM document and collection formats are a suitable means to encode and use multi-dimensional metadata for documents and document collections.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to formalize the semantics and the structure of a collection of heterogeneous documents, and how to put this formalized knowledge to good use.
the formalization of document collections, and the use of such formalized documents in the context of software engineering, and in particular, in software engineering education.
the question: "What is the best way of formalizing a set of documents, so that the formalization can serve as a basis for a number of different applications?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of RDFa for encoding metadata and the use of a flexible vocabulary for metadata relationships are a good way to cope with the challenges of multi-dimensional classification of document collections.
the use of RDFa-based extensions for markup formats is a promising and powerful way of integrating MKM with Semantic Web technologies and Linked Data.
RDFa is the best choice for the formalization of the document markup in our example, and that the MKM format is the most suitable choice to formalize the collection metadata.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show the feasibility of a flexible, extensible and interoperable approach for formalizing document and collection metadata, and that this approach is particularly suited to the needs of Software Engineering.
the formalization and reuse of knowledge in Software Engineering is a very promising application area for MKM.
we have shown that RDFa can be used to extend MKM formats to support a wide range of metadata dimensions, and that this is a promising direction for the future of MKM.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a document markup language can support a wide variety of document classification dimensions by means of metadata relationships, which can be used to enrich document browsing and search, to export Linked Data, and to enable the use of document collections as knowledge bases for software engineering.

the Semantic Web can be used to provide a flexible, extensible and scalable solution to the management of the metadata of collections of documents, and that RDFa can provide a simple and effective way to encode this information into the documents themselves.
a flexible, multi-dimensional, metadata-based formalization of document and collection structure is a promising approach for MKM in Software Engineering.
